Date of Notice: 2026-08-09
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-05
Service: Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
Treating Surgeon: Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), as stated in your Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-09. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I disagree with this determination and ask that it be reversed based on the clinical record summarized below and the criteria in Premera Medical Policy 7.01.590, "Shoulder Arthroplasty" (Effective Date: April 1, 2026; Last Revised: March 23, 2026).

That policy states that "Total shoulder arthroplasty may be considered medically necessary for joint disease when ALL of the following criteria are met," including a documented diagnosis, a treatment-need element, an imaging element, and two conservative-treatment elements. I address each below.

**1. Documented diagnosis**
The policy requires "a documented diagnosis of one of the following: Degenerative joint disease (DJD), Osteoarthritis (OA), Rheumatoid arthritis (RA), Traumatic arthritis, Avascular necrosis." Dr. Reyes's clinical findings (complete loss of glenohumeral joint space, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, flattened glenoid) are the radiographic hallmarks of glenohumeral osteoarthritis. I ask that the record be reviewed together with the surgeon's formal diagnosis of [diagnosis/ICD-10 code as documented in the surgical record] to confirm this element is met.

**2. Treatment need (disabling pain / functional disability ≥ 3 months)**
The policy requires treatment need due to "Disabling pain for at least 3 months duration" or "Functional disability which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living for at least 3 months duration." My record documents 14 months of progressive shoulder pain unrelieved by rest, and I am currently unable to reach overhead, dress without assistance, or sleep on the affected side. On examination, active forward elevation is limited to 90 degrees and external rotation to 10 degrees, with glenohumeral crepitus. This far exceeds the 3-month threshold in the policy.

**3. Imaging evidence**
This is the element cited in the denial, and it is squarely met. The policy requires "Radiographic or imaging evidence (e.g., X-ray, CT, MRI) of destructive degenerative joint disease of the shoulder in the 12 months prior to surgery as evidenced by ONE or more of the following: Irregular joint surfaces, Glenoid sclerosis, Glenoid osteophyte changes, Flattened glenoid, Cystic changes in the humeral head, Joint space narrowing." My shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary views) dated 2026-05-27 — within the required 12-month window — show "complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and a flattened glenoid." This documents at minimum three of the six qualifying findings listed in the policy: joint space narrowing, glenoid osteophyte changes, and flattened glenoid, with subchondral sclerosis directly corresponding to the policy's "glenoid sclerosis" finding. The policy requires only ONE such finding; my imaging shows multiple. I therefore ask that this element of the denial be reconsidered, as the imaging in the file satisfies the plan's own published criterion.

I also note that CT imaging confirmed an intact rotator cuff, which is clinically relevant because it supports the appropriateness of a standard total shoulder arthroplasty (rather than a reverse construct), consistent with the pathway under which this request was submitted.

**4. Three-month trial of medication/injection management**
The policy requires "Documentation of three months of failed non-operative conservative management as demonstrated by a trial of one or more of the following: Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics, Intra-articular injection of corticosteroids as appropriate." My record documents NSAID therapy for 6 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-22 that provided only 2 weeks of partial relief. This exceeds the policy's 3-month requirement.

**5. Six-week trial of physical measures**
The policy requires "A 6 week trial of one or more of the following physical measures under the direction of a healthcare professional: Physical therapy, Activity modification, Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises." My physical therapy discharge note documents 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-05-05 through 2026-07-14), 20 visits, focused on range-of-motion and periscapular strengthening — exceeding the 6-week minimum.

I further note that Premera's own policy states: "Total shoulder, reverse total shoulder, or hemi-arthroplasty is considered not medically necessary when the above medical necessity criteria are not met." As shown above, the criteria are met, and the sole basis stated in your denial letter — that "imaging findings ... do not support medical necessity" — is not supported by the imaging report in the file, which documents multiple qualifying findings under the policy's own imaging criterion.

I am enclosing/have asked my surgeon's office to submit the following supporting records with this appeal:
- Shoulder radiograph report dated 2026-05-27 and CT report
- Physical therapy discharge summary (2026-05-05 to 2026-07-14, 20 visits)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection dated 2026-05-22)
- Clinical/exam notes documenting range-of-motion limitations and functional impairment
- Surgeon's operative plan and diagnosis documentation from Dr. Reyes

Based on this record, I respectfully request that Premera Blue Cross reverse the denial and authorize CPT 23472, total shoulder arthroplasty, as medically necessary under Medical Policy 7.01.590.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of the expected timeframe for a decision. If any additional information is needed, please contact me at the phone number or email above, or my surgeon's office at [surgeon's office phone/fax]. If a delay in decision would jeopardize my health or ability to regain function, I ask that this appeal be treated as expedited, and I authorize you to contact Dr. Reyes directly to support that request if needed.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Skyler Ellison
Member ID: W656322877

Enclosures: [list of supporting medical records enclosed]

cc: Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery [office address/fax]
